rederive.effect: Sets the smallest minibatch size that uses the early launch of hardware attention. A minibatch with at least this many token jobs prepares and launches hardware attention before the K/V saves of the current token. A smaller minibatch saves K/V first and then prepares and launches (Note at h/tron/models/model.hpp:95-109, select_hw_attention_launch_phase at h/tron/models/model.hpp:159-163). The value 1 means always early. A value above every batch size means always late.

The first use is in a forward pass, when the first attention job is prepared (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2460-2461). It is not at program start. So a program with a bad value starts, loads the model, and aborts later.

rederive.audience_reason: It is a performance tuning value of the scheduler in rinzler and runtron, and a bad value stops the service.
rederive.default: Unset: 100000000 tokens (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1838). This is in practice no limit.
rederive.disagreement: Vague on the outcome of a bad value. cpp-tron.json says that with 0 or a negative value 'that loop adds no token to the pass' and stops there. The code goes on: build_forward_plan returns false with no token job, and forward() fails TRON_ASSERT 'Scheduler stuck: no work scheduled but not finished' (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2020-2025). So an empty value, non-numeric text, 0 or a negative number aborts the process at the first forward pass that has a token to schedule. The document must state this. Parsing, default and effect agree.
rederive.effect: Sets the soft limit on the number of live tokens that one forward pass of a scheduler takes. At the limit the tree walk stops adding tokens to the pass (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2410-2413). The first K/V token of a page and a listener-only token are admitted only below the limit (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2191, :2543). A lower value gives smaller forward passes and more of them.
rederive.empty_value: atoi gives 0. The result is the same as for an invalid value: the process aborts at the first forward pass that has work.
rederive.how_to_check: none found. No log line prints the limit. The Perfetto instant event 'forward args' of the category scheduler shows the number of token jobs of each pass (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2071-2074), which stays at or near the limit under load.
rederive.interactions: When max_minibatches of the model config is above 0, the limit is the smaller of the variable and max_minibatches x max_minibatch_size (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1839-1842). max_minibatches comes from rinzler -b / --max-batches (src/rinzler.cpp:4323-4325) or runtron --max-minibatches (src/runtron.cpp:969), merged with a bound from the model plugin (h/tron/models/config.hpp:112-118). The limit is soft: a page that already has K/V work is bound only by the hard capacity limit (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2181-2189). Each scheduler reads the variable when it is built. An EAGLE draft scheduler is a second scheduler and reads it again. The script bin/analyze-tps sets 100000 or 128 together with TRON_PER_USER_PROMPT_CHUNK_LIMIT to select a scheduling strategy (bin/analyze-tps:53-59).
rederive.invalid_value: The code does not reject any value. Non-numeric text gives 0. With 0 or a negative number, the check 'n_live_tokens >= live_token_limit' is true for the first token of every edge (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2410), so the pass gets no token job and reports that it did not schedule everything. forward() then fails TRON_ASSERT with the text 'Scheduler stuck: no work scheduled but not finished' (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2021-2025) and the process aborts. This result comes from reading the code. It was not run.
